plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.17
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the solid generated when the region under y = x^2 over [0, 2] is rotated about the line y = -1. The figure contains two linked views. Left (2D): the xy-plane showing the region R bounded above by the parabola y = x^2 and below by the x-axis between x = 0 and x = 2; the axis of revolution y = -1 is drawn as a horizontal red line, with a rotation arrow indicating revolution about it, and a representative washer cross-section at position x is sketched in gray. Right (3D): the resulting solid of revolution shown in perspective, with a visible central hole (from the inner radius of 1) and the parabolic outer surface. The figure illustrates the washer method: at each x, the cross-section is a washer with outer radius x^2 + 1 and inner radius 1, giving area pi((x^2 + 1)^2 - 1^2) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2), and the volume is computed by integrating this expression from 0 to 2.

interactions.label: Generating curve and axis
interactions.teaches: The same planar region can produce different solids when either the generating curve or the rotation axis changes, because the washer radii are measured from the axis to the two boundaries

interactions.label: Washer position x
interactions.teaches: At each x, the cross-section perpendicular to the axis is a washer whose outer radius is f(x)-c, inner radius is 0-c, and area is pi(R^2-r^2)
Rotating the view reveals that the right-hand object is a hollow solid of revolution, not a flat shaded profile

demo_steps.title: Near the start
demo_steps.narration: At x=0, the default curve has f(0)=0, so the outer and inner radii are both 1. The washer has zero thickness, matching the pinched left end of the solid.

demo_steps.title: Middle washer
demo_steps.narration: At x=1, the outer radius is 2 and the inner radius is 1, so the cross-section is a genuine washer with area 3π.

demo_steps.title: Largest washer
demo_steps.narration: At x=2, the outer radius is 5 and the inner radius is still 1. This gives the largest end washer, with area 24π.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use one math unit as approximately 0.8 world units in the left 2D view. The left plot occupies the left half of the frame: x from about -0.4 to 2.4, y from -2.4 to 4.8, with the y-axis near the left edge and the x-axis crossing horizontally through y=0. The default shaded region is bounded by y=x^2, y=0, x=0, and x=2; fill it light blue #c7e7f3 at about 65% opacity, with the curve in bright blue #249ed8 and stroke width about 4 px. The vertical boundary at x=2 is dark gray/black. The rotation axis y=c defaults to y=-1 and is a thin red line #ff5555 running horizontally from the left labels through the gap and through the center of the 3D solid. The representative washer in the left view is centered on the red axis at the selected x; draw it as a gray translucent annulus in the plane perpendicular to the x-axis, projected as a vertical ellipse: outer radius R=f(x)-c and inner radius r=0-c. For the right solid, place a separate 3D group on the right side, aligned so its central axis is the same screen-height as the red y=-1 line. Parameter t runs left-to-right from 0 to 2; map this to a world length of about 2.6 units. The radial directions are vertical Y and depth Z. For default f(x)=x^2, c=-1: outer radius R(t)=t^2+1, inner radius r=1, so the solid starts pinched at t=0 and expands to outer radius 5 at t=2. Compress the displayed 3D solid uniformly if needed so the end radius visually fits the frame; preserve the radius ratios 1:5. Outer surface color should be pale blue-gray #c8dce5 with transparency around 0.45; inner cylinder and end faces gray #bfc1c3 with metallic/rough shading; rim outlines medium gray #9da1a4. The 3D view should resemble the source: long axis horizontal, large annular end face on the far right, small neck on the left, central cylindrical hole visible through the solid.
interactionPlan.notes: Generate the 3D solid procedurally as surfaces of revolution about the horizontal axis y=c. For each sampled x in [0,2] and angle theta, outer surface point is (X_offset + scaleX*x, c + R(x)*cos(theta), depthScale*R(x)*sin(theta)); inner surface uses r=0-c. Use enough samples, e.g. 96 around the rotation and 100 along x, to make the parabolic surface smooth. Recompute the shaded 2D region, curve polyline, washer annulus, solid mesh, end annulus, and numeric radius/area readouts whenever the equation input changes. If the learner enters an axis c that is not below both y=0 and f(x) over the full interval, display a small inline warning that the simple washer formula R=f(x)-c, r=0-c assumes the axis lies below the region.

authoredContext: Find the volume of the solid generated when the region under the curve y = x2 over the interval [0, 2] is rotated about the line y =−1. Solution. First sketch the region and the axis of revolution; then imagine revolving the region about the axis (Figure 5.2.17). At each x in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, the cross section of the solid perpendicular to the axis y =−1 is a washer with outer radius x2 + 1 and inner radius 1. Since the area of this washer is A(x) = π([x2 + 1] 2 − 12 ) = π(x4 + 2x2 ) it follows by (3) that the volume of the solid is V = ! 2 0 A(x) dx = ! 2 0 π x4 + 2x2_x000b_ dx = π 1 5 x5 + 2 3 x3 _x0010_2 0 = 176π 15

discrepancies: The 3D solid on the right is darker and more opaque than the source, making the inner cylindrical hole read more like a filled rectangular block than a light translucent hollow cylinder.
The right-hand solid is somewhat compressed and lacks the clear light-gray end rim and subtle front/back elliptical depth cues visible in the source figure.
The representative washer on the left includes extra colored radius guide lines that are not present in the original textbook figure.
The curve and region are close, but the shaded region and labels are slightly smaller and more compact than in the source composition.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure accurately represents the washer-method setup and adds useful interactions, though the 3D solid is visually too dark and block-like compared with the lighter textbook rendering.
action_items: Lighten the materials of the 3D solid and reduce opacity/darkness so the hollow washer structure is clearer.
Add clearer front and rear elliptical rims to the inner cylinder and end washer to better match the source depth cues.
Reduce or restyle the extra radius guide lines in the 2D washer so they do not distract from the original figure.
